# Viability, search strategy and data extraction

Most dose-response meta-analyses fail here rather than at the model. This
chapter turns the checklist at the end of Chapter 1 into something you can run
against a real extraction sheet.

::: {.callout-warning}
Draft. The structure below is fixed and matches the class; the prose is being
written.
:::

## What makes a dataset viable

The three conditions, restated as data requirements: a quantitative exposure on
a common scale, enough levels per study, and enough reported per level to
reconstruct the within-study covariance.

## Counting exposure levels per study

Why three is the two-stage floor, and why a study with two levels argues for a
one-stage model rather than for exclusion [@crippa2019].

## The reference category problem

Studies rarely agree on a reference group. How to re-express estimates against a
common reference [@hamling2008], and the floating-variance alternative
[@easton1991].

## Harmonising doses across studies

Unit conversion, midpoint assignment for open-ended categories, and what to do
when the top category has no upper bound.

## What to extract, field by field

The extraction sheet: study, dose level, midpoint, cases, total, person-time,
effect estimate, interval, and the adjustment set.

## Search strategy

How a dose-response question changes the search, and why the filter is usually
looser than expected.

## Running the viability check

Using `dr_viability()` on the finished sheet, and reading its output as a
decision about which model to fit.
